title: Sports & Movement Categories
subtitle: Every sport is a set of rules about how you are allowed to move.
objectives: Sort sports into individual, dual and team
Explain invasion, net or wall, striking and target games
Name the three kinds of movement skill
Explain why the same skill transfers between sports
Explain what a national sport is and why it changes

cards.title: Sports are grouped twice, for two different reasons
cards.text: Once by how many people are on your side. Once by what the game actually asks you to do.

cards.title: Both ways of sorting, side by side
cards.text: Tap through. The first three are about numbers. The last three are about the task.

cards.title: Individual, dual, team
cards.text: This one is easy to read off. Count who shares the score with you.
points: **Individual:** the result is yours alone.
**Dual:** one against one, or two against two.
**Team:** a group with a shared score.
**Some sports are both**, like relay swimming.

question.text: Badminton singles is which kind of sport?
question.explain: Dual means one against one. It is also a net game, because the two sides are separated.

cards.title: Invasion, net, striking, target
cards.text: This grouping is more useful, because sports in the same group need the same thinking.
points: **Invasion:** you enter their half to score.
**Net or wall:** a barrier keeps you apart.
**Striking and fielding:** hit, then run.
**Target:** the goal does not move or resist.

cards.title: Boxing is dual, and it is a combat sport
cards.text: There is no net and no ball. What decides it is distance control, which is the same skill a fencer trains.
points: **Reach and footwork** set the whole fight.
**Combat sports** are their own category.
**Judged on hits landed**, not territory taken.
**Amateur bouts** are three rounds of three minutes.

question.text: Which of these is an invasion game?
question.explain: You cross into their half to score. Volleyball is a net game and archery is a target game.

cards.title: Good place to stop
cards.text: Part 2 is movement skills and the national sport. Move around before you carry on.

cards.title: Three kinds, and every sport mixes them
cards.text: Locomotor, non-locomotor and manipulative. The names sound technical and the ideas are simple.

cards.title: Move, hold, handle
cards.text: Locomotor moves you somewhere. Non-locomotor happens on the spot. Manipulative involves an object.
points: **Locomotor:** run, jump, skip, gallop.
**Non-locomotor:** twist, bend, stretch, balance.
**Manipulative:** throw, catch, kick, dribble.
**A layup uses all three** in two seconds.

cards.title: Skills transfer because the pattern is the same
cards.text: A throw and a punch are both a rotation that starts at the back foot and ends at the hand.
points: **Power comes from the ground up**, always.
**A boxer who plays volleyball** learns to spike fast.
**Balance trained anywhere** shows up everywhere.
**This is why cross-training works.**

question.text: Dribbling a basketball is which kind of movement skill?
question.explain: It involves handling an object. Running while you do it adds a locomotor skill on top.

cards.title: Arnis, since 2009
cards.text: Republic Act 9850 made arnis the national martial art and sport of the Philippines. It is stick fighting, and it is very old.
points: **Also called eskrima or kali.**
**Trained with rattan sticks**, then empty hands.
**Basketball is more popular**, but it is not the national sport.
**Popularity and official status** are different things.

cards.title: Game designers use these categories too
cards.text: A capture-the-flag mode is an invasion game. A fighting game is a dual combat sport with a fixed ruleset.
points: **The categories describe the problem**, not the sport.
**Same category, same tactics.**
**Spacing in a fighting game** is boxing's distance control.
**Learn the category and you learn faster.**

terms.def: The result belongs to one person alone.
One against one, or two against two.
You enter the opponent's territory to score.
A barrier separates the two sides.
A movement that takes you somewhere: run, jump, skip.
A movement that handles an object: throw, catch, kick.
The national martial art and sport, made official in 2009.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Individual, dual, team:** count your side.
**Invasion, net, striking, target:** the actual task.
**Locomotor, non-locomotor, manipulative.**
**Arnis is the national sport.** Basketball is the popular one.

quiz.text: Which of these is an individual sport?
quiz.explain: One person, one result. Doubles tennis is dual and the other two are team sports.
quiz.objective: Sort sports into individual, dual and team

quiz.text: Boxing is which kind of sport by numbers?
quiz.explain: One against one. It is also a combat sport, judged on hits rather than territory.
quiz.objective: Sort sports into individual, dual and team

options: You enter the opponent's territory to score
You aim at a fixed target
You hit an object then run
quiz.explain: Basketball, football and rugby all work this way.
quiz.objective: Explain invasion, net or wall, striking and target games

quiz.text: Volleyball belongs to which task category?
quiz.explain: A barrier keeps the two sides apart. Badminton and tennis are in the same group.
quiz.objective: Explain invasion, net or wall, striking and target games

quiz.explain: The goal does not move and does not resist you. Bowling and darts are the same.
quiz.objective: Explain invasion, net or wall, striking and target games

quiz.explain: Locomotor skills take you somewhere. Twisting and balancing happen on the spot.
quiz.objective: Name the three kinds of movement skill

quiz.explain: It happens on the spot, without travelling and without an object.
quiz.objective: Name the three kinds of movement skill

quiz.text: Kicking a ball is which kind of skill?
quiz.explain: Manipulative skills handle an object. Throwing, catching and dribbling are the same group.
quiz.objective: Name the three kinds of movement skill

quiz.text: A basketball layup uses more than one kind of movement skill.
quiz.explain: True. Running is locomotor, the jump and reach add non-locomotor, and the ball makes it manipulative.
quiz.objective: Explain why the same skill transfers between sports

quiz.text: Why does training in one sport often help in another?
options: The underlying movement patterns are shared
All sports use the same rules
quiz.explain: A throw and a punch are both a rotation driven from the back foot. That is why cross-training works.
quiz.objective: Explain why the same skill transfers between sports

quiz.text: What is the national martial art and sport of the Philippines?
quiz.explain: Made official by Republic Act 9850 in 2009. It is also called eskrima or kali.
quiz.objective: Explain what a national sport is and why it changes

quiz.text: The most popular sport in a country is automatically its national sport.
quiz.explain: False. Basketball is far more popular in the Philippines, but arnis holds the official status.
quiz.objective: Explain what a national sport is and why it changes

teacher.summary: Week 7 covers the PE strand on sports and movement categories. The lesson teaches both classification systems and is explicit that the task-based one (invasion, net, striking, target) is the more useful of the two, because sports inside a category share tactics. The movement-skill section connects directly to his boxing training: the transfer argument is real biomechanics, not encouragement. Arnis is included with its actual legal basis, and the distinction between official status and popularity is made explicitly, because that is a common exam trap.
discussion: Ask him to place three sports he knows into both classification systems at once.
Ask what tactics basketball and football share, and why.
Ask him which movement skills a single boxing combination uses.
Ask why a country would name a national sport that most people do not play.
teacher.extension: Have him invent a new game and specify its category, its three movement skills, and one rule that makes it different from an existing sport in the same group.
misconceptions: 'Individual sport means no team.' Athletes in individual sports often compete for a team score as well.
'Net games and invasion games are basically the same.' The barrier changes every tactic in the game.
'Basketball is the national sport of the Philippines.' It is the most popular. Arnis is the national sport.
'Movement skills are only for young children.' Every sport is built from the same three categories.
